chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Does normal environmental noise make your tinnitus louder?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Is your tinnitus constant during the day? Are there interruptions, and if so, for how long?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Is your tinnitus distressing? From the beginning or only later?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Are you particularly sensitive to noise?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Can you influence the tinnitus through self-directed measures such as shifting attention, relaxation or other means?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Do you or other people notice that you hear or understand worse?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Has the tinnitus occurred together with hearing loss and/or ear pressure?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Has the tinnitus occurred together with severe spinning vertigo?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Can the tinnitus be influenced by certain head postures or jaw movements?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Can the tinnitus be influenced by certain jaw/chewing muscle tension?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Can the tinnitus be influenced by physical exertion?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: What medication are you currently taking?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Have you been treated with medication for serious infections (e.g. tuberculosis, meningitis, myocarditis, pneumonia, malaria, etc.) or malignant diseases and if so, with what?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Have you been irradiated because of a malignant disease in the head and neck area?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Do you have any cardiovascular or metabolic diseases?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Are there any indications of other disorders and comorbidities (see Table 1)?
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: The determination of the severity of tinnitus is important and recommended for the therapy indication in individual cases. The classification of the degree of severity according to Biesinger et al. [65] is a pragmatic classification oriented to the clinical situation and takes into account the effect of the ear noise in the professional and private sphere:
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Grade 1: The tinnitus is well compensated, no suffering.
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Grade 2: The tinnitus mainly appears in silence and is disturbing in the case of stress and strain.
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Grade 3: Tinnitus leads to permanent impairment in the private and professional sphere. Disturbances occur in the emotional, cognitive and physical spheres.
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: Grade 4: The tinnitus leads to complete decompensation in the private sphere and occupational disability.
chunks.section: 5. Appendix / 5.3 Appendix 3: Medical history questions and clinical severity classification

chunks.text: The evidence tables for the treatment procedures examined in this guideline and the methodological details can be found on the AWMF website [321].
